# shadow/valid-event-names

Require JSX event attributes to name real DOM events and take functions.

`recommended` `fixable` `has suggestions`

## Why

A misspelled handler (`onClik`) is just an unknown attribute: no listener is attached and nothing complains. Handler names are accepted in any casing (`onClick`, `onclick`), and React's capture spelling (`onClickCapture`) listens in the capture phase like `oncapture:click`. Handlers must be functions: the compiler refuses a string, and `onClick={setCount(1)}` runs at render time and passes its result.

## Incorrect

```tsx
<button onClik={save}>x</button>
```

```tsx
<button onClick="save()">x</button>
```

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useSignal(false);
const view = <button onClick={setOpen(true)}>x</button>;
```

```tsx
<input on:Input={update} />
```

## Correct

```tsx
<button onClick={save}>x</button>
```

```tsx
<button oncapture:click={log} onKeyDownCapture={log}>x</button>
```

```tsx
<input on:input={update} on:my-custom-event={custom} />
```

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useSignal(false);
const view = <button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>x</button>;
```

## Autofix and suggestions

A DOM event name with capital letters after `on:` or `oncapture:` is fixed to lower case. Suggestions rename an unknown `onX` that is within two edits of a known handler, and turn a lower-case `onclickCapture` into `oncapture:click`. String handlers and handlers called at render are only reported.

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/valid-event-names`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/valid-event-names */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/valid-event-names */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. For a non-standard event a DOM element really fires but the JSX typings do not list yet; prefer `on:name`, which accepts any event name, before disabling.

## Notes

- Only DOM elements (lower-case tags) are checked; components define their own `onX` props.
- `on:` and `oncapture:` accept any event name (custom events), but DOM event names must be lower-case.
- React's capture spelling of a known handler (`onClickCapture`) binds the capture phase, as the compiler does; a lower-case `onclickCapture` is reported with a suggestion to use `oncapture:click`.
- The list of known handler names mirrors the JSX typings of `@shadow-js/web` (kept in sync by a test).

## Messages

- `unknownEvent`: `{{name}}` is not a DOM event handler. No listener will be attached.
- `didYouMean`: Rename to `{{replacement}}`.
- `captureSuffix`: `{{name}}` is React's capture syntax. Use `oncapture:{{event}}` to listen in the capture phase.
- `useCapture`: Use `oncapture:{{event}}`.
- `badCasing`: DOM event names in `{{name}}` must be lower-case: `{{replacement}}`.
- `stringHandler`: `{{name}}` is given a string. Event handlers must be functions (`{{name}}={handler}`).
- `calledHandler`: `{{name}}` is given the result of a call, which runs while rendering. Pass a function: `{{name}}={() => ...}`.
